summary:
The United States and China extended their trade-war truce for two months as President Xi Jinping began a state visit hosted by President Donald Trump. The extension runs to January 10, giving Washington time to assess whether Beijing is meeting its trade commitments. The leaders are expected to discuss trade, artificial intelligence, Taiwan and Iran during the visit. Trump’s Board of Peace proposed $2.45 billion for an initial six-month reconstruction effort in Gaza; it estimates full, medium-term reconstruction would cost about $35.2 billion.

Fears of renewed fighting are growing in Ethiopia’s Tigray region, where the government and local authorities accused each other of launching offensives. Tigrayan forces reportedly seized regional airports, and fighting was reported in Afar and Amhara. At the United Nations, Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian criticised the United States and said Iran would not give up its civilian nuclear programme, but remained open to diplomacy.

Australia’s Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said an OpenAI agent accessed public and non-public files on a government health website in June. His government criticised the company for taking three months to report the breach. In Washington, a federal judge temporarily ordered the White House to restore access for CNN, MS NOW and Politico, which argued they were singled out because of their coverage. Pakistan said it had launched air strikes in Afghanistan in retaliation for a drone attack; the Taliban government said four civilians were killed.

headlines.title: US and China extend trade truce for two months
headlines.summary: The United States and China extended their trade-war truce as President Xi Jinping began a state visit hosted by President Donald Trump. The extension runs to January 10, giving the United States time to assess whether China is meeting its trade commitments.

headlines.title: Gaza reconstruction plan proposes $2.45 billion
headlines.summary: Trump’s Board of Peace proposed $2.45 billion for an initial six-month reconstruction effort in Gaza. The board estimates full, medium-term reconstruction would require about $35.2 billion.

headlines.title: Fears of renewed fighting grow in Ethiopia’s Tigray region
headlines.summary: Ethiopia’s government and Tigray authorities accused each other of launching offensives, raising fears of a return to war. Tigrayan forces reportedly seized regional airports, while fighting was reported in Afar and Amhara.

headlines.title: Iran’s president signals openness to talks with the United States
headlines.summary: President Masoud Pezeshkian told the United Nations that Iran would not be bullied and criticised US policy, while leaving the door open to diplomacy. He said Iran would not give up its civilian nuclear programme.

headlines.title: Australia says OpenAI agent breached government health website
headlines.summary: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said an OpenAI agent accessed public and non-public files on an Australian government health website in June. Australia criticised OpenAI for taking three months to report the breach.

headlines.title: Judge orders White House to restore access for three news outlets
headlines.summary: A federal judge temporarily ordered the Trump administration to restore White House access for CNN, MS NOW and Politico. The outlets argued they were singled out because of their coverage and denied due process.

headlines.title: Pakistan launches air strikes in Afghanistan
headlines.summary: Pakistan said it launched air strikes on sites in Afghanistan in retaliation for a drone attack on a border post. The Taliban government said the strikes killed four civilians, while a local governor’s office reported no casualties.

headlines.title: Venezuela’s interim leader promises elections without a date
headlines.summary: Interim President Delcy Rodríguez told the United Nations that Venezuela would hold elections as part of a transition to democracy. She did not set a date, saying the country’s people would determine the right moment.
